Course Contents: 
Building Quantity Surveying Training report in prescribed format is to be submitted at the time of ISE. 
 Following points should be covered during the Training. 
 Detailed estimate of Framed Structure. 
 Rate Analysis of ten civil engineering items. 
 Schedule of reinforcement (Bar Bending Schedule) 
 
Preparing detailed estimate for any one of the following: 
A. A stretch of a road about 1 Km. long including earthwork. 
B. A reach of canal about 1 Km. long. 
C. A factory shed of steel frame.

Course Description: 
This course is designed for Second Year B. Tech. Civil Engineering students who are taking exit from 
04 Year B. Tech. Program. The course offers an introduction to the field of Transportation Engineering. 
This course makes students aware of the importance of transportation in nation development & available 
career options.  
Course Learning Objectives: 
1. Understand road development process. 
2. Understand the rail infrastructure components.  
3. Describe the components of Aviation Infrastructure.  
4. Discuss the elements of waterfront structures.  
5. Explain the importance of tunnels for infrastructure development.

Course Contents: 
Unit 1: Introduction to Highway Engineering 
CO: 1 & 2 
 
Brief History of Road Development in India, Objects of Planning, Planning Surveys and 
their Interpretation. Introduction to NHAI Agency, IAHE, NHIDCL, NHDP Phases, 
MSRDC. Current schemes of government such as Bharatmala - I & II, SARDP-NE, LWE. 
Terrain classification, design speed, vehicular characteristics, highway cross-section 
elements. Introduction to Traffic Engineering: Definition, objectives and scope of Traffic 
Engineering, Traffic Regulation and Control.  
08 Hrs. 
Unit 2: Geometrics of Highways 
CO: 1 & 4 
 
Sight distance: introduction to sight distance, reaction time, analysis of safe sight distance, 
analysis of overtaking sight distance.  
Horizontal alignment: Highway alignment & Surveys, curves, super elevation and its 
provision, radius at horizontal curves, widening of pavements at horizontal curves.  
Vertical alignment: different types of gradients, grade compensation on curves, summit 
curves & valley curves.  
11 Hrs. 
Unit 3: Introduction to Railway Engineering 
CO: 1 & 4 
 
Elements of permanent way – Rails, Sleepers, Ballast, rail fixtures and fastenings, Track 
Stress, coning of wheels, creep in rails, defects in rails. Route alignment surveys, 
Geometrics of railways, gradient, super elevation, widening of gauge on curves, Points and 
Crossings. Construction & Maintenance methods.  
08 Hrs.

Unit 4: Introduction to Airport Engineering 
CO: 1 & 3 
 
Air transport characteristics, airport classification, airport planning: objectives, components, 
layout characteristics, criteria for airport site selection and typical airport layouts, Passenger 
Facilities and Services, Runway and Taxiway Markings, Pavement and lighting. 
06 Hrs. 
Unit 5: Introduction to Dock & Harbor Engineering  
CO: 1 & 3 
 
Definition of Basic Terms, Planning and Design of Harbors, Requirements, Classification, 
Harbor Layout and Terminal Facilities, Coastal Protection Works. Dry dock and wet dock 
differentiation. 
06 Hrs. 
Unit 6: Introduction to Tunnel Engineering 
CO: 1 & 3 
 
Introduction, Size and Shape of The Tunnel, Tunneling Methods in Hard Rock & Soft 
Material, Tunnel Lining, Tunnel Lighting, Drainage and Ventilation, Tunneling using 
Tunnel Boring Machine, Trenchless Construction Method (TCM). 
06 Hrs.

Course Pre-Requisite: 
Engineering Mechanics, Solid Mechanics, Structural Analysis 
Course Description: 
The Fundamentals of Structural Design & Detailing course introduces students to the fundamental 
principles of reinforced concrete (RC) design, including stress-strain behavior, permissible stress, and 
different design philosophies. It covers the limit state method for designing beams, slabs, columns, and 
footings, following IS 456:2000 guidelines.  
Course Learning Objectives: 
1. Understand the fundamental concepts of stress-strain behavior, permissible stresses, safety factors, 
and design philosophies in reinforced concrete structures. 
2. Apply the principles of the limit state method to analyze and design singly and doubly reinforced 
beams, slabs, staircases, columns, and footings. 
3. Analyze the structural behavior of RC elements under different loading conditions, including shear, 
bond, torsion, and serviceability requirements. 
4. Interpret and implement IS 456:2000 guidelines for designing reinforced concrete structures while 
considering practical constraints and safety measures.
